acceptance.given: A TC-D1 change proposes a write whose target resolves to an account-boundary path.

oracle.expected: The write attempt is rejected and the resulting evidence records that account-boundary protection blocked the operation.
forbidden: Replay or Consumer permission is treated as authorization for account repair.
oracle.observable: The governance-policy decision and filesystem state show rejection with no account-boundary mutation.

acceptance.then: Account boundaries remain unchanged and the operation terminates unsuccessfully.
acceptance.when: During validation of the proposed TC-D1 write, evaluate the target against the account-boundary policy before applying any mutation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise an account-path write request and assert the policy rejects it before mutation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject any TC-D1 write targeting an account boundary; replay or Consumer permission cannot authorize account repair.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No account data or schema is changed; denied writes remain backward compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposed account-boundary write -> policy rejection -> unchanged account boundary
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The authorization decision is reject and no account-boundary file content changes.

acceptance.given: Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages participate in one evaluation or rollback workflow.

oracle.expected: Inspection or execution evidence demonstrates independently controlled mutable state and evidence containers for each listed component.
forbidden: Any listed component shares mutable state with another listed component.
Cross-component state or evidence mutation changes another component's execution or result.
oracle.observable: The isolation check records distinct state identities/containers and detects attempted cross-component mutation.

acceptance.then: Each component operates with isolated mutable state, preventing cross-component contamination or false success.
acceptance.when: During unit or integration inspection of the replay workflow, execute the isolation witness and inspect the resulting state/evidence boundaries.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the NFR-4 isolation witness with an attempted cross-component state mutation and require the boundary check to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Give each listed component independently controlled mutable state and evidence, rejecting cross-component mutation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve replay result schemas; isolate internal mutable state without changing external route contracts.

slice_hint.state_transition: shared workflow state -> component-local state/evidence -> cross-component mutation rejected
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The isolation witness observes distinct mutable-state boundaries and rejects any cross-component write.

acceptance.given: The Consumer Manifest contains one or more non-empty entries with applicable route transitions.

oracle.expected: Every applicable enable, disable, rollback, and re-enable transition completes for each non-empty Consumer entry, with the required route identity and result evidence.
forbidden: A non-empty Consumer entry omits an applicable transition.
A route transition is marked complete without the real Consumer call and its observation.
oracle.observable: The replay receipt contains a per-entry transition record covering every applicable route transition and its observed result.

acceptance.then: All applicable route transitions are complete for 100% of non-empty Consumer Manifest entries.
acceptance.when: Execute the Consumer route-transition verification against the frozen manifest and reconcile each entry with its applicable transitions.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the Consumer transition selector with one applicable transition omitted or unreachable and require a runtime failure marker.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Invoke and record every applicable route transition for each non-empty Consumer entry, including rollback baseline observations.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing Consumer receipt fields while adding complete transition observations.

slice_hint.state_transition: manifest entry pending -> real transition calls -> per-entry completed or failed
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every non-empty manifest entry has a recorded successful observation for each applicable transition; any omission yields unsuccessful evaluation.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result has reached a successful terminal result.

oracle.expected: The successful Replay Result includes an independently produced Validator Capability verification bound to the replay identity.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result lacks independent Validator Capability verification.
Validator Capability is accepted solely from candidate-supplied or self-reported data.
oracle.observable: The receipt contains an independent Validator Capability verification record whose identity matches the replay binding.

acceptance.then: Validator Capability is independently verified before the successful Replay Result is accepted as evidentiary output.
acceptance.when: After replay execution reports success, perform the independent Validator Capability verification and inspect its binding in the result receipt.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the successful-replay selector with independent Validator Capability verification absent or mismatched and require a runtime failure marker.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require an independent, replay-bound Validator Capability verification before a successful Replay Result is considered valid evidence.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Successful-result receipts remain non-authorizing; missing independent capability verification converts success to invalid evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: replay success candidate -> independent capability verification -> accepted evidentiary success or rejection
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A successful replay result is emitted only when the independent Validator Capability verification exists and matches the replay identity.
